original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Classify square links on two fixed disjoint normal-form blocks inside a pattern-dimension-5 no-edge pool, and decide whether the irreducible image-dimension-7 witness is unique up to coordinate permutation.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package changes that premise to open question 2 of the pattern-dimension-5 no-edge witness: whether every irreducible complete pool of pattern dimension 5 and joint-image dimension 7 is a coordinate permutation of the seven projectors in open PR #7237. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838, #6921, #6962, and the open #7237 witness.
bottleneck_link: Side result. A second coordinate realization shows that the dimension-7 witness is not unique, so a later argument cannot quote uniqueness as a classification. It does not change a paid identity or the selected kappa. The original native acceptance gate remains unmet.
stop_rule: Stop once the odd-fresh family, the disjoint-support reducibility statement, and the width 7-9 censuses are checked. Do not start an upper bound or a non-square width-8 enumeration.
evidence: PROOF.md Theorem 1 shows that every odd fresh size on the two hubs gives an irreducible seven-projector pool of pattern dimension 5 and image dimension 7. Theorem 2 shows that every other square meeting each block in at most one coordinate has the same pool shape and image dimension but is reducible, with an explicit invariant subspace. The fresh-size-3 pool is not a coordinate permutation of the fresh-size-1 witness. Section 10 records exhaustive censuses: all 8128 idempotents at width 7, and all odd squares at widths 8 and 9. verify.py repeats those checks. The fiber lemma is cited for the even coset at every width and is not reproved.

open_questions.question: Does every complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 5 have total joint image at most 7?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The odd-fresh family attains 7, so 6 is too small, but it does not prove an upper bound. The zero-edge quotient bound is still 31.
open_questions.first_step: Test a one-dimensional extension of one pattern space of dimension 6, and look for an invariant-subspace argument that is not restricted to two normal-form blocks.
open_questions.blocked_by: Theorems 1 and 2 classify only squares that meet each of two fixed blocks in at most one coordinate.

open_questions.question: Is there an irreducible image of dimension 7 whose pattern space contains no two disjoint normal-form blocks?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Such a pool would be a coordinate class different from every odd-fresh link, including the fresh-size-1 witness.
open_questions.first_step: Decide whether every irreducible image-7 pattern space of dimension 5 contains at least one normal-form triple.
open_questions.blocked_by: The Grassmannian of 5-planes in the 42-dimensional space of 7 by 7 zero-diagonal matrices is not a feasible enumeration.

open_questions.question: At width 8, does a non-square idempotent extension of these two blocks have irreducible image dimension 7?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The width-7 census includes non-squares and finds only the fresh-size-1 square. Width 8 was enumerated for squares only.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate all (2^8-1)2^7 = 32640 idempotents at width 8 with the same complete-pool test used at width 7.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package did not run that finite census. A partial sample would not answer the question.
